fact: In standard cricket, each bowling over consists of exactly 6 legal deliveries.
Sachin Tendulkar is the all-time leading run-scorer in international cricket and the only player to score 100 international centuries.
The West Indies won the inaugural Men's Cricket World Cup in 1975, defeating Australia at Lord's.
A batsman can be dismissed in ten official ways in cricket, with Bowled, Caught, and LBW (Leg Before Wicket) being the most common.
Virat Kohli holds the record for the most centuries in One Day Internationals (ODIs), scoring his 50th ODI ton during the 2023 World Cup.
The historic rivalry between England and Australia in Test cricket is commemorated by a small terracotta urn known as The Ashes.
Brian Lara holds the record for the highest individual score in Test cricket history with 400 not out against England at Antigua in 2004.
Rohit Sharma holds the record for the highest individual score in ODI cricket, scoring 264 runs off 173 balls against Sri Lanka at Eden Gardens in 2014.
India won its first ever ICC Cricket World Cup in 1983 under the captaincy of Kapil Dev, defeating the two-time defending champions West Indies.
The pitch in cricket has a standard length of 22 yards (20.12 meters) between the bowling and batting stumps.
Muttiah Muralitharan holds the world record for the highest number of Test wickets with 800 dismissals in 133 matches.
The inaugural ICC Men's T20 World Cup was held in South Africa in 2007, with India winning the final against Pakistan in Johannesburg.
The first official Test match in cricket history was played between Australia and England at the Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG) in March 1877, which Australia won by 45 runs.
Sir Donald Bradman retired with a Test career batting average of 99.94, needing just 4 runs in his final innings at The Oval in 1948 to average 100, but was dismissed for a duck.
Jim Laker of England took 19 wickets for 90 runs against Australia at Old Trafford in 1956, the best bowling analysis in a single Test match.
Under MCC Law 31.7, if a batsman is 'Timed Out', the incoming batter must be ready to face the ball within 3 minutes (or 2 minutes in T20/ODI playing conditions) of the previous dismissal.
Only three bowlers in Test history have taken all 10 wickets in an innings: Jim Laker (1956), Anil Kumble (1999), and Ajaz Patel (2021).
Yuvraj Singh hit 6 sixes in an over off Stuart Broad in the 2007 T20 World Cup, scoring the fastest half-century in international cricket in just 12 balls.
